summary: Refunds that time out at the payment gateway are now sent again, up to three attempts in all, waiting 500 ms and then 1 s in between. Every attempt carries the same idempotency key, made from the refund id, so the gateway pays a refund once however many times it arrives. Any other error, and a timeout on the last attempt, reaches the caller as before.

claims.text: Refund requests that time out at the gateway are tried up to three times.
claims.evidence: The new test "gives up after three attempts" passes on head: five timeouts in a row make three posts, then the timeout is thrown.

claims.text: Nothing changes for a refund that succeeds first time.
claims.evidence: The existing test "sends the refund" passes on base and head with one post.
Two new tests. Both pass on head and fail on base. Neither covers a timeout after the gateway already took the refund.

claims.text: Every attempt of one refund carries the same idempotency key.
claims.evidence: The lost-reply probe now passes: two posts, one refund paid.
